invariants.rule: Publication-state flag. Placeholder/stub chapters are `indexed: false`; published chapters with real content are `indexed: true`. Both states must be explicit and set on every chapter — never omit it. PRIMARY PURPOSE: draft-release-notes.mjs emits a "chapter added" entry when a chapter transitions from false to true, so leaving a real chapter fieldless breaks that explicit false→true signal. SECONDARY EFFECT: consumers read `indexed !== false`, so `indexed: false` also keeps stub ("coming soon") chapters out of the verse search index (build-verse-index.mjs), out of the sitemap, and robots-noindex’d (see shouldIndex in [slug].astro) — desired, since placeholder pages should not be searchable. The chapter validator additionally uses `indexed: false` to recognize a stub and skip its "no verse markers" check, so stubs must carry it. For a real chapter, `true` and absent behave identically in both consumers; `true` is required only to keep the release-notes lifecycle an explicit two-state (false→true) machine rather than one relying on field absence.

Each verse marker id (id="vN" on <sup class="vn">) must appear exactly once per chapter. A verse that spans a paragraph break keeps its marker only at its start; the continuation paragraph carries NO marker (this is what makes the number appear once). Duplicate ids are invalid HTML — epubcheck rejects them and the #vN deep-link anchor becomes ambiguous — so a repeated verse number is always a bug, never a style choice. The chapter validator enforces uniqueness as an error (any verse id appearing more than once fails validation and blocks the pre-commit hook).
